title: `MIN % -1` returns 0 at 2.0.1; it raised at 2.0.0
verdict: `MIN % -1` is 0 at every integer width at 2.0.1, as the reference says; at 2.0.0 it raised `Overflow in division`; the SQL writes the case out at both versions
description: The probe of `BIGINT % BIGINT` (`engines/duckdb/replay/probes.json`) over the 64-bit bounds finds one row that moved: `-9223372036854775808 % -1` raised `Out of Range Error: Overflow in division of -9223372036854775808 / -1` at 2.0.0 (`duckdb-R15-int-modulus`) and is 0 at 2.0.1. At 2.0.1 the candidate `ERROR` of `on_division_by_zero` matches all 121 rows of the probe (the NULL candidate for the rows where `error_on_division_by_zero` is off), where at 2.0.0 none did. Only the 64-bit width was re-probed; the narrower widths were not.

The change is error-side (D70): DuckDB raises less than at 2.0.0, and gives the reference's value. The profile's `min_mod_neg_one` row still says `ERROR`, which stays a safe bound at 2.0.1 (a plan verified under the engine's own semantics is not claimed to avoid a raise that no longer happens). The lowering writes the case out (`MIN % -1 written out`), so a plan runs the same at both versions.
